new.title: Admire the carved façade of Notre-Dame-la-Grande
new.desc: Romanesque church in Poitiers whose west front, carved in the early 12th century, is covered with biblical scenes, a bestiary and plant motifs. A major restoration ran from 1992 to 2004 to clean pollution and salt damage from the stone.
new.tip: Best at dusk, when the façade is lit. Interior access has been limited by renovation work, so check the tourist office before going in.
new.q: Église Notre-Dame la Grande, Place Charles de Gaulle, Poitiers

new.title: Step inside the Baptistère Saint-Jean
new.desc: Reputed to be one of the oldest surviving Christian buildings in France, built in the 4th century on Roman foundations and enlarged in the 7th. Its walls keep 12th-century frescoes, and it is now a small museum.
new.tip: Allow 30 minutes. It stands a few steps from the cathedral.
new.q: Baptistère Saint-Jean, Rue Jean Jaurès, Poitiers

new.title: See the Crucifixion window of Poitiers Cathedral
new.desc: Gothic cathedral begun in the 1160s under Henry II Plantagenet and Eleanor of Aquitaine. Its central apse holds a 12th-century Crucifixion stained-glass window studied by art historians since the 19th century.
new.tip: Morning light on the east window is best. Entry is free.
new.q: Cathédrale Saint-Pierre, Rue de la Cathédrale, Poitiers

new.title: Walk the Salle des Pas Perdus of the Dukes' Palace
new.desc: The Palais des Ducs d'Aquitaine, now the law courts, kept its great hall rebuilt around 1191-1204 under Eleanor of Aquitaine. The Maubergeon tower was rebuilt around 1380 under Jean de Berry.
new.tip: The hall is free to enter in public hours; the Maubergeon tower opens on some afternoons and weekends.
new.q: Palais des Ducs d'Aquitaine, Place Alphonse Lepetit, Poitiers

new.title: Browse the Musée Sainte-Croix
new.desc: Museum on the site of the former Sainte-Croix abbey, with archaeology, fine arts and local history from Gallo-Roman Poitiers onwards. It also stages temporary exhibitions.
new.tip: Entry is free on Tuesdays and the first Sunday of the month; check current opening hours.
new.q: Musée Sainte-Croix, 3 bis Rue Jean Jaurès, Poitiers

new.title: Visit the Romanesque Église Saint-Hilaire-le-Grand
new.desc: Romanesque church on the presumed burial site of Hilary of Poitiers, a stop on the Camino and part of the UNESCO Santiago de Compostela routes listing since 1998. The choir and ambulatory remain Romanesque, while the nave was largely rebuilt in the 19th century.
new.tip: Interior access has been restricted by works in recent years, so check ahead; the exterior and apse are always worth a look.
new.q: Église Saint-Hilaire-le-Grand, Rue Saint-Hilaire, Poitiers

new.title: Descend to the tomb of Saint Radegonde
new.desc: The church holds the tomb of Queen Radegonde, who died in 587, in a crypt reached by a 19th-century staircase. The tomb was desecrated in the Wars of Religion and burnt bones were re-sealed in 1565; votive plaques cover the walls.
new.tip: Pilgrims come here around 13 August, her feast day.
new.q: Église Sainte-Radegonde, Place Sainte-Radegonde, Poitiers

new.title: Stroll the terraces of the Parc de Blossac
new.desc: Nine-hectare public park laid out around 1770 by the Count of Blossac above the Clain valley, with a French garden, a rock garden on the old ramparts, an English garden from 1905 and a small zoo.
new.tip: Free, open daily; the Chemin de la Cagouillère leads down to the river.
new.q: Parc de Blossac, Rue de Blossac, Poitiers

new.title: Browse the Marché Notre-Dame
new.desc: Covered halls and open-air stalls on Place Charles de Gaulle beside Notre-Dame-la-Grande, with market gardeners, bakers, fishmongers and caterers. Most halls trade Tuesday to Saturday and the Saturday outdoor market is the biggest.
new.tip: Go on Saturday morning; the market closes on Monday and most traders pack up by 13:00.
new.q: Marché Notre-Dame, Place Charles de Gaulle, Poitiers

new.title: Watch Révélation light the façade of Notre-Dame-la-Grande
new.desc: Free summer show by the company Spectaculaires projecting colour and sound onto the Romanesque façade, held on Place Charles de Gaulle. In 2026 it ran nightly in summer.
new.tip: Shows start around 22:30 in high summer; arrive early for a place on the square.
new.q: Place Charles de Gaulle, Notre-Dame-la-Grande, Poitiers

new.title: Buy farci poitevin at Maison Édouard
new.desc: Charcuterie shop in central Poitiers run by Édouard Normand from a seven-generation family, known for farci poitevin made with pork and green cabbage or chard, plus herb sausages and rillettes.
new.tip: Closed Monday and Sunday morning. Ask for a slice of farci to eat cold with bread.
new.q: Maison Édouard (Boucherie Normand), 10 Rue Carnot, Poitiers

new.title: Order farci poitevin at Le Poitevin
new.desc: Long-running restaurant on rue Carnot serving Poitou-Charentes dishes such as farci poitevin, gigot d'agneau and filet de boeuf sauce charentaise, at about 30 euros a head.
new.tip: Call ahead for hours and booking.
new.q: Le Poitevin, 76 Rue Carnot, Poitiers

new.title: Dine on seasonal Vienne produce at Vingelique
new.desc: Restaurant at 37 rue Carnot rated by Gault&Millau, cooking seasonal French dishes with ingredients from local producers around the Vienne.
new.tip: Open for dinner Tuesday to Saturday; book ahead. Menus run about 30 to 40 euros.
new.q: Vingelique, 37 Rue Carnot, Poitiers

new.title: Eat lunch in a Jesuit chapel at Les Archives
new.desc: Brasserie installed in a 19th-century Jesuit chapel that once housed the regional archives, with a vegetarian menu and a well-known lunch formula.
new.tip: Book for lunch, when the set menu is the draw.
new.q: Les Archives, 14 Rue Édouard Grimaux, Poitiers

new.title: Drink and eat from food trucks at La Guinguette Pictave
new.desc: Riverside bar on the Île de Tison on the Clain, opened in 2018, with a dozen food trucks, shuffleboard, darts and cornhole.
new.tip: Evenings on a sunny day; beer from about 4.90 euros.
new.q: La Guinguette Pictave, Chemin de Tison, Poitiers

new.title: Paddle the Clain from Tison
new.desc: TEX' rents canoes, kayaks and paddleboards by the hour, half-day or day from a base on Chemin de Tison in Poitiers. The longest trip is a weekend descent of about 13 km from Ligugé to Tison.
new.tip: Check hours and book before going; trips run in warm months.
new.q: Chemin de Tison, Poitiers

new.title: Taste butter broyé du Poitou at Goulibeur
new.desc: Maker of broyé du Poitou since 1976 in Poitiers, a pure-butter shortbread with no yeast or preservatives. The firm holds the Entreprise du Patrimoine Vivant label and has a shop on its production site.
new.tip: Hours differ by source; call 05 49 41 34 75 before visiting.
new.q: Goulibeur, 10 Rue Victor Grignard, Poitiers

new.title: Buy a tourteau fromagé at Jahan
new.desc: Bakery founded in 1971 at Saint-Benoît and taken over by the Jahan family in 1988, known for the black-topped goat-cheese tourteau fromagé and Croquants de Saint-Benoît.
new.tip: Closed Sunday; the shop is near the Poitiers-Biard airport roundabout.
new.q: Tourteaux Jahan, 1 Rue Bessie Coleman, Rond-point de l'aéroport, Poitiers-Biard, Poitiers

new.title: Spend a day at Futuroscope
new.desc: Multimedia theme park opened in 1987 at Chasseneuil-du-Poitou, with over 40 attractions on 70 hectares. Chasseurs de Tornades opened in 2022 and a children's area, Futuropolis, has about twenty rides.
new.tip: Hours vary by season; shows are included in the ticket and the A10 exit 28 is two minutes away.
new.q: Futuroscope, Chasseneuil-du-Poitou

new.title: See the Romanesque murals of Saint-Savin Abbey
new.desc: The abbey church holds some 420 to 460 square metres of Romanesque wall paintings in the nave, porch and crypt, with scenes from Genesis and the Apocalypse. It was inscribed on the UNESCO list in 1983 and nicknamed the Romanesque Sistine Chapel.
new.tip: Look up in the nave vault for the Noah and Tower of Babel scenes.
new.q: Abbaye de Saint-Savin, Place de la Libération, Saint-Savin

new.title: Explore the Château d'Harcourt in Chauvigny
new.desc: Best preserved of the five castles that crown the rocky spur of Chauvigny above the Vienne. It forms part of the guided visit of the medieval town with the château baronnial and the Saint-Pierre collegiate church.
new.tip: Combine with the walk through the medieval upper town.
new.q: Château d'Harcourt, Chauvigny

new.title: Climb the Gouzon keep for views over Chauvigny
new.desc: 12th-century keep of the Château de Gouzon, classified as a historic monument, which since 1993 houses an industrial archaeology space on Chauvigny stone, porcelain and steam engines. The tower gives a view over the whole town.
new.tip: Check opening times at the tourist office.
new.q: Donjon de Gouzon, Chauvigny

new.title: Watch the birds-of-prey show Les Géants du Ciel
new.desc: Open-air falconry show staged in the ruins of the château baronnial in Chauvigny, with eagles, falcons, owls and vultures flying over the arena. Aviaries can be seen before and after.
new.tip: Season runs roughly April to September; the site is only open with a show ticket.
new.q: Les Géants du Ciel, Château baronnial, Chauvigny

new.title: Pedal a rail bike over the Vienne viaducts
new.desc: VéloRail runs pedal-powered rail bikes on a disused railway line from Chauvigny, crossing viaducts above the Vienne. The full trip is about 17 km return and takes one to two hours.
new.tip: Booking is strongly recommended; the mid-trip option costs about 10 euros per adult.
new.q: VéloRail de Chauvigny, 10 Rue de la Folie, Chauvigny

new.title: Eat bistronomic local food at Saint-Pierre et le Loup
new.desc: Bistronomic table in Chauvigny's upper town with a veranda terrace facing the Saint-Pierre collegiate church, serving home-made dishes based on local and organic produce.
new.tip: Check current hours and book in season.
new.q: Saint-Pierre et le Loup, Chauvigny

new.title: Climb to the ruined castle of Angles-sur-l'Anglin
new.desc: Medieval castle on a rocky spur above the Anglin, with 11th-century origins and changes in the 12th and 15th centuries; Du Guesclin retook it from the English in 1372. The village is one of the Plus Beaux Villages de France.
new.tip: Self-guided visit; the valley view is the highlight.
new.q: Château d'Angles-sur-l'Anglin, Angles-sur-l'Anglin

new.title: Discover the Roc-aux-Sorciers sculpted frieze
new.desc: Magdalenian rock shelter with carvings about 15,000 years old, nicknamed the Lascaux of sculpture. The original frieze is closed to protect it, so visitors see a full-size reconstruction at the interpretation centre.
new.tip: Book the visit ahead; allow about an hour.
new.q: Roc-aux-Sorciers, Route des Certeaux, Angles-sur-l'Anglin

new.title: Take the waters at La Roche-Posay Thermal Centre
new.desc: Dermatology spa town with a thermal centre of four establishments, including Thermes du Connétable and Spa Source. The 13 degree spring water holds selenium, silica and strontium and is used for eczema and psoriasis.
new.tip: Spa Source (58 avenue des Fontaines) is open year-round for day visits.
new.q: Les Thermes du Connétable, Avenue du Docteur Benjamin Bord, La Roche-Posay

new.title: Meet the bonobos at La Vallée des Singes
new.desc: Primate park at Le Gureau in Romagne, founded by Wim Mager of Apenheul, with wooded island enclosures. It holds over 30 species and one of the largest bonobo groups in captivity.
new.tip: Open from mid-March to mid-November; book tickets ahead in high season.
new.q: La Vallée des Singes, Le Gureau, Romagne

new.title: Wander Montmorillon's City of Writing
new.desc: Cité de l'écrit et des métiers du livre fills the medieval Brouard quarter with about twenty antiquarian booksellers, calligraphers, illuminators and bookbinders since 2000. Free to enter, with workshops and guided visits.
new.tip: Look for the Latin and Chinese calligraphy and illumination studios.
new.q: Cité de l'écrit, 3 Rue Bernard Harent, Montmorillon

new.title: Taste the original Montmorillon macarons at Rannou-Métivier
new.desc: Macaron house founded around 1920, rated by Gault&Millau, with an Almond and Macaroon Museum opened in 2003. The traditional recipe has passed through five generations.
new.tip: Visits end with a tasting; buy a box of the soft almond macarons.
new.q: Maison Rannou-Métivier, 32 Boulevard de Strasbourg, Montmorillon

new.title: Climb the Tour Carrée of Loudun
new.desc: Square 12th-century keep, 31 metres high, last main survivor of a fortress dismantled under Richelieu, listed since 1877 and renovated from 2017. It overlooks the town and has a medieval-style garden.
new.tip: Open roughly April to November.
new.q: Tour Carrée, Loudun

new.title: Relive Aliénor and the Hundred Years War at Monts-sur-Guesnes
new.desc: Medieval castle turned interactive history attraction (Historial du Poitou), opened in May 2022 in its new form, with about ten rooms in two buildings on Eleanor of Aquitaine and the Hundred Years War.
new.tip: Confirm hours at chateau-monts-sur-guesnes.com or by phone, 05 49 22 89 81.
new.q: Château de Monts-sur-Guesnes, 1 Allée des Marronniers, Monts-sur-Guesnes

new.title: Visit the fairytale ruin of La Mothe-Chandeniers
new.desc: 13th-century moated castle of the Bauçay family, gutted by a fire in 1932 and bought back in 2017 by thousands of online co-owners from 115 countries. It is a ruin open to visitors in season.
new.tip: Check mothe-chandeniers.com for open days and volunteer events.
new.q: Château de la Mothe-Chandeniers, Les Trois-Moutiers

new.title: Visit Saint-Martin Abbey at Ligugé
new.desc: Founded in 361 by Saint Martin, regarded as the oldest monastery of the West still in activity. The grounds and church are free to enter, with weekend guided visits for a contribution.
new.tip: Guided visit on weekends at 15:00; hours vary, check before going.
new.q: Abbaye Saint-Martin, Place Saint-Martin, Ligugé

new.title: Follow the Mélusine legend in Lusignan
new.desc: Medieval town tied to the fairy Mélusine, who was said to have built the ramparts in a night; a sculpture of her with outstretched wings adorns the chevet of Notre-Dame church.
new.tip: Start at the church and follow the ramparts to the promenade de Blossac.
new.q: Église Notre-Dame-et-Saint-Junien, Lusignan

new.title: Hike the Sentier de Mélusine around Lusignan
new.desc: Easy loop of about 9 km and 3 hours passing where Raymondin met Mélusine, the ramparts, a postern gate and the Tour Mélusine, with many shaded sections.
new.tip: Wear walking shoes; the route passes the Vonne valley.
new.q: Sentier de Mélusine, départ parking de la base de loisirs, Lusignan

new.title: Wander the Merovingian necropolis of Civaux
new.desc: Enclosure built from upright Merovingian sarcophagus lids, dating from 500 to 750, once four times larger. Guided tours from the archaeological museum cover the Roman sanctuary, baptistery and the church with a seven-sided apse.
new.tip: Tours start at the museum; check hours in the low season.
new.q: Nécropole mérovingienne, Civaux

new.title: Tour the Musée Bernard d'Agesci in Niort
new.desc: Niort art and history museum managed with the Donjon by Niort Agglo; during the Donjon works one ticket (5.50 euros) opens both sites.
new.tip: Visit takes about two hours.
new.q: Musée Bernard d'Agesci, 26 Avenue de Limoges, Niort

new.title: Browse the Halles de Niort
new.desc: 1885 covered market hall with about 55 traders, plus an open-air market on its terraces. Thursday, Saturday and Sunday are the big market days; it opens Tuesday to Sunday.
new.tip: Go before 13:00 on Saturday.
new.q: Halles de Niort, Place des Halles, Niort

new.title: Glide through the Venise Verte by punt from Coulon
new.desc: Coulon is the main gateway to the Marais poitevin, with the largest number of embarcadères and a Maison du Marais poitevin. Flat-bottomed barques glide along duckweed-covered canals under ash and poplar.
new.tip: One-hour trips cost about 12 to 16 euros per adult.
new.q: Maison du Marais poitevin, Coulon

new.title: Row the quiet canals from Arçais
new.desc: Family-run Embarcadère Bardet-Huttiers, founded in 1976, rents boats and canoes and runs guided trips April to October, with an island picnic area reached by boat.
new.tip: Quieter than Coulon in high season; outside April to October by reservation only.
new.q: Embarcadère Bardet-Huttiers, Route de Chauvillon, Arçais

new.title: Walk the village-street of La Garette and the marsh
new.desc: La Garette (Sansais) is a typical Marais mouillé village-street with old maraîchin houses along a canal; a trail runs through the marsh towards Le Vanneau.
new.tip: Best by bike or on foot; combine with a boat trip.
new.q: La Garette, rue des Gravées, Sansais-La Garette

new.title: Dine at L'Auberge de l'Écluse in Coulon
new.desc: Restaurant opposite the Sotterie lock in the heart of the Marais poitevin, serving regional cuisine based on local products.
new.tip: Book for weekends; check menu and hours.
new.q: L'Auberge de l'Écluse, 328 route des Bords de Sèvre, La Sotterie, Coulon

new.title: See the crypt of the abbey church of Saint-Maixent
new.desc: Abbey church of the Benedictine abbey of Saint-Maixent, whose crypt holds 6th- and 7th-century sarcophagi of Saint Maixent and Saint Léger. The abbey buildings became barracks and the NCO school in 1880.
new.tip: Check access to the crypt with the tourist office.
new.q: Abbatiale, Rue de l'Abbatiale, Saint-Maixent-l'École

new.title: Walk the Rue de la Vau-Saint-Jacques in Parthenay
new.desc: Medieval town whose 13th-century Porte Saint-Jacques with two almond-shaped towers marks the start of the Vau-Saint-Jacques street, lined with half-timbered houses and tied to the Camino.
new.tip: Guided tours of the medieval town are run by the town heritage service.
new.q: Porte Saint-Jacques, Rue de la Vau Saint-Jacques, Parthenay

new.title: Explore Oiron castle and its Curios & Mirabilia collection
new.desc: Renaissance château built by the Gouffier family, home to a contemporary art collection of about 80 commissioned works, plus a gallery with Troy murals ranked second only to Fontainebleau.
new.tip: Managed by the Centre des Monuments Nationaux; check hours at chateau-oiron.fr.
new.q: Château d'Oiron, 10 Rue du Château, Oiron

new.title: Visit Saint-Médard and the old town of Thouars
new.desc: Romanesque church below the Château des ducs de La Trémoïlle, rebuilt in the 17th century. The town also holds the medieval Tour du Prince-de-Galles.
new.tip: The château is now a school; walk the ramparts.
new.q: Église Saint-Médard, Thouars

new.title: Discover the Antonine commandery of Saint-Marc-la-Lande
new.desc: Village grown around the Antonine commandery established around 1260; its early 16th-century collegiate church is called the finest Flamboyant Gothic building in Deux-Sèvres.
new.tip: Small village; combine with the Bocage des Antonins nature reserve.
new.q: Collégiale Saint-Antoine, Saint-Marc-la-Lande

new.title: See the three Romanesque churches of Melle
new.desc: The Romanesque triad of Saint-Savinien, Saint-Pierre and Saint-Hilaire; Saint-Hilaire is the largest and counts on the Camino listing.
new.tip: Allow two hours to see all three.
new.q: Église Saint-Hilaire, Melle

new.title: Descend into the Silver Mines of the Frankish Kings
new.desc: Oldest silver mines open to visitors in Europe, with about 350 metres of the 30 km of tunnels visitable. In the Carolingian period Melle was the empire's largest silver mine, with a mint.
new.tip: Underground temperature is cool; bring a layer.
new.q: Mines d'argent des Rois Francs, Melle

new.title: Stroll the gardens of Celles-sur-Belle abbey
new.desc: Royal abbey founded as an Augustinian priory and made an abbey around 1137-1140; Louis XI funded the church rebuilding. The one-hectare French garden dates from the 1990s.
new.tip: Guided visits, a 3D film and underground galleries.
new.q: Abbaye royale, Celles-sur-Belle

new.title: Walk around the Coudray-Salbart fortress
new.desc: Fortress built at the end of the 12th century and reworked in the early 13th century at Échiré; volunteers have been restoring it since 1961 and it hosts a medieval festival.
new.tip: Free open visits happen on some weekends; check dates.
new.q: Château du Coudray-Salbart, Échiré

new.title: Meet lynx and wolves at Zoodyssée
new.desc: Departmental wildlife park in Chizé forest at Villiers-en-Bois with European fauna such as Eurasian lynx and grey wolf, and a breeding programme for the European pond turtle.
new.tip: Open 10:00 to 17:00 or 18:00 depending on season.
new.q: Zoodyssée, Villiers-en-Bois

new.title: Taste AOP chabichou goat cheese at Fromagerie des Gors
new.desc: Producer near Melle of Chabichou du Poitou AOP, the local goat cheese. Sales Monday to Saturday mornings; visits by appointment.
new.tip: Call 05 49 27 06 58 before going.
new.q: Fromagerie des Gors, Rue de la Chagnée, Melle
